newsitem.title: USA: CME traders say USDA cattle data bearish deferreds.
newsitem.headline: CME traders say USDA cattle data bearish deferreds.

text.p: CME traders said Friday's monthly Cattle on Feed Report issued by the U.S. Department of Agriculture was constructive for nearby live cattle futures but bearish for deferred contracts.
"The bull spreads should work," one trader said, noting May marketings in the seven primary cattle feeding states were larger than expected but placements were also greater than expected.
Dean Witter analyst Dale Benson said the nearby June contract could open 0.25 cent a lb higher based on the data with August off 0.25 cent and October down 0.50 cent.
USDA put May placements in the seven leading states at 126 percent of a year ago versus an average estimate of 117.2 percent in a Reuter survey of analysts and a range of 110.5 to 124.0 percent.
May marketings were estimated by USDA at 104 percent of a year ago compared with an average analyst estimate of 99.0 percent and a range of 97.0 to 102.0 percent.
USDA put the number of cattle-on-feed in the leading seven states at 113 percent of a year ago, in line with an average analyst estimate of 113.2 percent and well within the 111.5 to 114.0 range.
